oewn-02541527-s.learner: warm and friendly in a polite way.
examples: Though they disagreed, the neighbours stayed cordial and always said good morning.

connotation.why: polite warmth that may stop short of real closeness

oewn-07083250-n.learner: language that is strong and works well on the people who hear or read it.
examples: But little had she dared to hope that so much love and eloquence awaited her there.

connotation.why: admires the speaker's skill where 'speech' would not

oewn-01812324-s.learner: hurt, upset, or annoyed in your feelings.
examples: In a softened tone she declared herself not at all offended
Mr. Collins, much offended, laid aside his book

oewn-04845958-n.learner: bold, even proud, behaviour that you have no right to.
examples: This match, to which you have the presumption to aspire, can never take place.
There was nothing of presumption or folly in Bingley

connotation.why: condemns someone for overstepping their place

oewn-05901963-n.learner: an idea that is accepted as true without being questioned.
examples: The whole plan rests on the presumption that prices will stay low.

oewn-01228051-n.learner: a rude act in which someone takes a liberty they should not take.
examples: Calling her by her first name was a presumption she did not forgive.

connotation.why: names the act as a breach of manners

oewn-05789344-n.learner: in law, a conclusion that something is true, drawn from other facts that have been proved, admitted, or accepted by the court.
examples: Because he had been missing for seven years, the court made a presumption that he was dead.

oewn-00983053-s.learner: fast; moving, or able to move, at high speed.
examples: Conjectures as to the meaning of it, rapid and wild, hurried into her brain
The rapid river carried the little boat away.

oewn-00982888-s.learner: done or happening in a short time.
examples: She made a rapid recovery after the operation.

oewn-13799556-n.learner: an amount of something that is there for people to use.
examples: a servant was despatched to Longbourn, to acquaint the family with her stay, and bring back a supply of clothes.

oewn-13584725-n.learner: the offering of goods and services for people to buy.
examples: When supply is low and demand is high, prices go up.

oewn-01059124-n.learner: the act of giving or providing something.
examples: The company is in charge of the supply of water to the town.

oewn-10820913-n.learner: a person who can write and who has written something.
examples: To Catherine and Lydia neither the letter nor its writer were in any degree interesting.
her feelings towards its writer were at times widely different.

oewn-10813654-n.learner: a person whose job is writing books, stories, articles, or similar things for money.
examples: She worked as a writer for a travel magazine.

oewn-00232532-s.learner: better in quality, or more excellent.
examples: There is not a finer county in England than Derbyshire.
Nothing in even our author is finer and more delicately touched than the change of his demeanour

oewn-00021147-s.learner: happy and willing to do favours for other people.
examples: By nature inoffensive, friendly, and obliging, his presentation at St. James's had made him courteous.
Lady Catherine's behaviour was most friendly and obliging.

oewn-10329281-n.learner: a person who is paid to fight for a country that is not their own.
examples: The king paid mercenaries from abroad to defend his castle.

connotation.why: fighting for pay rather than loyalty, against plain 'soldier'
